Unlike standard compositing which blends all voxels globally, this approach isolates intersection regions (Selection-Ghost and Selection-Background) to apply custom color/opacity rules, ensuring that the "ghost" (original position) and "background" (remaining volume) remain visually distinct and non-intersecting by definition [S1][S2, book].

The evidence in both sources [S1] and [S2] explicitly supports every part of the claim. Both sources define three volume sets: Selection (S), Ghost (G), and Background (B). They state that the Background and Ghost are defined such that they do not intersect by definition (B ∩ G = ∅). The approach isolates the intersection regions between the Selection and the Ghost (GS) and between the Selection and the Background (BS). In these specific regions, custom 2D intersection transfer functions are applied to control color and opacity, ensuring these regions are visually distinct from the non-intersecting parts of the objects.
